text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz says an early election is the last resort to the ongoing political turmoil.
- Ruling Islamist deputies welcome a campaign by rightist papers to declare which ministers sign the bill for eight years uninterrupted, compulsory education.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan was not briefed on the evaluation of common threats to Israel and Turkey after a visit by Israel's foreign minister to Ankara last month.
- As workers celebrate May Day, figures show that wage rises in the last six years have remained well below inflation.
- Modern Turkey's first Islamist leader Erbakan signed a military statement identifying religious "fundamentalism" as the prime threat for Turkey.
- May Day will be celebrated by rallies held throughout Turkey.
- Privatisation is deadlocked because of political instability.
- United Nations General Secretary Kofi Annan says face to face talks between the parties on the divided island of Cyprus expected in June.
